title: British Food: A Changing Reputation
titleZh: 英国食物：正在改变的声誉

sentences.text: What comes into your mind when you think of British food?
Probably fish and chips, or a Sunday dinner of meat and two vegetables.
But is British food really so uninteresting?

Even though Britain has a reputation for less-than-impressive cuisine, it is producing more top class chefs who appear frequently on our television screens and whose recipe books frequently top the bestseller lists.

paras.zh: 当你想到英国食物时，你会想到什么？可能是炸鱼薯条，或者一顿肉配两种蔬菜的周日晚餐。但英国食物真的如此乏味吗？尽管英国因其不太出色的烹饪而享有声誉，但它正在培养出更多顶级厨师，这些厨师频繁出现在我们的电视屏幕上，而且他们的食谱书经常位居畅销书榜首。

sentences.text: It's thanks to these TV chefs rather than any advertising campaign that Britons are turning away from meat-and-two-veg and ready-made meals and becoming more adventurous in their cooking habits.
It is recently reported that the number of those sticking to a traditional diet is slowly declining and around half of Britain's consumers would like to change or improve their cooking in some way.
There has been a rise in the number of students applying for food courses at UK universities and colleges.
It seems that TV programmes have helped change what people think about cooking.

paras.zh: 正是多亏了这些电视厨师，而不是任何广告宣传活动，英国人正在远离肉配两种蔬菜和即食餐，在烹饪习惯上变得更加勇于尝试。最近据报道，坚持传统饮食的人数正在缓慢下降，大约一半的英国消费者希望在某种程度上改变或改进他们的烹饪。申请英国大学和学院食品课程的学生人数有所增加。看来电视节目已经帮助改变了人们对烹饪的看法。

sentences.text: According to a new study from market analysts, 1 in 5 Britons say that watching cookery programmes on TV has encouraged them to try different food.
Almost one third say they now use a wider variety of ingredients than they used to, and just under 1 in 4 say they now buy better quality ingredients than before.
One in four adults say that TV chefs have made them much more confident about expanding their cookery knowledge and skills, and young people are also getting more interested in cooking.
The UK's obsession with food is reflected through television scheduling.
Cookery shows and documentaries about food are broadcast more often than before.
With an increasing number of male chefs on TV, it's no longer "uncool" for boys to like cooking.

paras.zh: 根据市场分析师的一项新研究，五分之一的英国人说看电视烹饪节目鼓励他们尝试不同的食物。几乎三分之一的人说他们现在使用的食材种类比以前更广泛，近四分之一的人说他们现在购买的食材质量比以前更好。四分之一的成年人说电视厨师让他们对扩展烹饪知识和技能更加自信，年轻人也对烹饪越来越感兴趣。英国对食物的痴迷通过电视节目安排反映出来。烹饪节目和关于食物的纪录片比以前播出得更频繁。随着电视上男性厨师数量的增加，男孩喜欢烹饪不再"不酷"了。
